rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when someone gives in to a temptation or desire.

example.english: On holidays, I like to indulge myself by eating a big piece of chocolate cake.
example.traditional: 假日我鍾意放縱自己，食一大件朱古力蛋糕。
example.jyutping: gaa3 jat6 ngo5 zung1 ji3 fong3 zung3 zi6 gei2 sik6 jat1 daai6 gin6 zyu1 gu2 lik6 daan6 gou1

rows.note: Use this conversational pattern when the emphasis is on being unable to resist and then doing the tempting action.

example.english: I couldn't resist the freshly baked egg tarts, so I decided to indulge and eat two.
example.traditional: 我一見到啱啱出爐嘅蛋撻，就忍唔住食咗兩個。
example.jyutping: ngo5 jat1 gin3 dou2 ngaam1 ngaam1 ceot1 lou4 ge3 daan6 taat1 zau6 jan2 m4 zyu6 sik6 zo2 loeng5 go3

rows.note: Use this colloquial construction when someone gives another person whatever they want or lets them have their way.

example.english: Our son wants ice cream, and we indulge him; we are really spoiling him.
example.traditional: 阿仔想食雪糕，我哋就晒佢，真係太縱容喇。
example.jyutping: aa3 zai2 soeng2 sik6 syut3 gou1 ngo5 dei6 zau6 saai3 keoi5 zan1 hai6 taai3 zung3 jung4 laa3
